rubrics.criterion: After the patch, no component of the C implant's channel-facing code declares its own copy of a channel-identity value: no stage-, transport-, or crypto-local variable, record, or value-yielding function in the agent's C sources still carries a private binding of the server address, wire port, cover path, query-parameter name, cookie name, or pre-shared secret outside the configuration layer.
rubrics.rationale: This task's entire failing surface is the set of private re-declarations of channel identity that accumulated across the agent; leaving even one in place means that value class still has a second owner, which is precisely the reported maintenance failure.

rubrics.criterion: Each channel-identity value class (server address, wire port, cover path, query key, cookie name, pre-shared secret) is declared exactly once in the agent's configuration layer, and every consumer — the three beacon stages, the HTTP transport operations they drive, and both payload-crypto directions — obtains its value from that single declaration, so editing a value there propagates to all of the implant's traffic.
rubrics.rationale: The maintainer's reported problem is that re-pointing the channel in its configuration no longer moves all of the implant; success is defined by the one-edit-per-change property, which is the semantic outcome graded here rather than any specific code shape.

rubrics.criterion: The initial check-in stage's request operands (host, port) and its parsing of the session cookie both derive from the single configuration declarations, and the polling loop's request operands do the same, with any stage-local address hooks or ports that shadowed them removed.
rubrics.rationale: Routing the configuration through the stages requires rewiring the actual call sites that build the initial request and parse its Cookie-shaped response and the poll request; these call sites are where a half-done repair strands a stage on stale values that differ from the rest of the agent only under the next channel change.

rubrics.criterion: The results stage builds its request URL and endpoint (cover path, query-parameter name, host, and port) from the configuration declarations, and any stage-local endpoint record or path/query bindings that held private copies are retired or converted to reference the configuration.
rubrics.rationale: The results stage composes the exfil URL piece by piece, so moving it onto the configuration owner is a distinct, separately verifiable change from the registration/polling wires; a repair that fixes the other stages but leaves exfil pinned strands exactly the traffic the maintainer says he could not account for.

rubrics.criterion: The HTTP transport connects to and renders Cookie headers using the configuration-declared channel identity: any transport-level fallback address and any cookie-name composition inside the transport derive from the configuration declaration rather than being pinned in the transport source, with its callers continuing to pass real host values as before.
rubrics.rationale: The transport is the layer that actually formats the wire request, and this case put a private address default and private cookie-name rendering inside it; leaving them there recreates the second owner inside the most shared code path even after the stages themselves are cleaned.

rubrics.criterion: Both payload-crypto directions obtain the pre-shared secret from the same single configuration declaration, so encrypt_buffer and decrypt_buffer remain interoperable through one owned key specification.
rubrics.rationale: This case split the protocol's key specification between the encrypt side and a decrypt-side binding; re-unifying it is a distinct obligation from the HTTP-side work because a mismatch here produces silently unreadable tasking rather than a visible connection failure.

rubrics.criterion: The scaffolding that existed only to hold the private copies is removed or repurposed together with its use sites: stage-local pin variables, the endpoint record type used to carry a private host/port pair, and any address-yielding helper either disappear from the agent's sources or now read from the configuration declarations.
rubrics.rationale: The private copies in this instance live in visible stage-idiosyncratic scaffolding (pin variables, a record type, a one-line getter); a coherent repair carries that scaffolding away with the copies instead of leaving a second, now-misleading vocabulary of the channel behind.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor does not leave injected artifacts dangling: no once-used stage-pin variable declaration without remaining users, no orphaned endpoint record type, and no un-called address-yielding helper function remain declared in the agent's sources.
rubrics.rationale: This instance introduced declared, addressable pieces of channel vocabulary at file and function scope; deleting the uses while keeping the declarations is the most likely incomplete cleanup path in C, where unused statics and unused struct types compile silently and remain for the next maintainer to misread.

rubrics.criterion: For the same configuration values, the refactor does not alter any request bytes the implant would previously have issued: the initial check-in URL keeps its cover-path/query-key order and payload suffix, polling and results URLs keep their composition, the Cookie header carries the session value in the same name=value form with no doubled or dropped cookie name, and the Host header, method, header set, and header order are unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: All of this agent's channel traffic is hand-composed strings whose exact bytes are the deployment's cover contract; URL or Cookie-header composition drift is the concrete regression a consolidation of this shape can silently produce, and it is invisible to any test that does not render a request.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor does not leave the two crypto directions on divergent key material or altered key-derivation paths: a payload encrypted by the implant's encrypt path must decrypt correctly through its decrypt path with unchanged output lengths and padding semantics, with neither direction deriving from a declaration that changes under the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The case deliberately put a copy of the secret on the decrypt side only, so a repair that moves one direction but not the other, or re-derives the key differently on one side, breaks payload interop in a way that manifests only at tasking time, long after the build is green.

rubrics.criterion: Session-cookie lifecycle is preserved: the same session value extracted from the check-in response ends up in later request headers, without truncation, without the cookie name prefixed twice, without the terminator or attributes of the Set-Cookie field leaking into the stored value, and without an empty session being sent.
rubrics.rationale: This instance re-bound the cookie name at both the parse site and the transport header-rendering site; because two places must agree on one string, a repair that fixes only one side produces doubled or missing cookie names — the exact class of half-consolidation the prompt warns about.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidation does not create a second home for channel identity: the working channel values do not end up re-declared in some new internal constants file, build-time define set, or stage-shared header separate from the configuration layer the agent already has, leaving the next channel change a guessing game between two owners.
rubrics.rationale: A tempting repair for this case is to gather the scattered copies into one new place rather than onto the existing configuration owner; that would still scatter the specification across two homes in the repository, which is this task's specific failure mode, not a generic style concern.
